+## Change data capture
+
+Postgres change data capture (CDC) uses logical replication to stream row-level changes to PostHog. This relies on two database-level objects:
+
+- A **replication slot**, which retains write-ahead log (WAL) changes until PostHog consumes them.
+- A **publication**, which identifies the tables included in logical replication.
+
+The database user must have privileges to create and use replication slots and publications. Tables can use different sync modes, and CDC behavior applies only to tables configured for CDC sync.
+
+Replication slots retain WAL data until consumed, so an inactive or slow CDC sync can cause WAL lag. Excessive WAL lag can delay or interrupt CDC sync and may also increase disk usage on your database.
+

+## Pausing and resuming subscriptions
+
+Each subscription has an **enabled** toggle. By default, new subscriptions are enabled. Turning the toggle off pauses delivery without deleting the subscription, so you can keep the configuration and re-enable it later.
+
+When you re-enable a subscription, PostHog immediately schedules a confirmation delivery and resets the next delivery date. If the delivery target is still invalid, PostHog blocks re-enabling until the underlying issue is fixed.
+
+## Automatic disabling for invalid delivery targets
+
+If a subscription's delivery target becomes permanently invalid — for example, the Slack integration used by the subscription is removed, or the target type is not supported — PostHog automatically disables the subscription, logs an activity entry, and sends an email notification to the subscription owner.
+
+Disabled subscriptions are skipped by scheduled deliveries. To resume delivery, fix the underlying issue (for example, reconnect Slack or change the subscription target), then re-enable the subscription.
+

+.. setting:: broker_pool_acquire_timeout
+
+``broker_pool_acquire_timeout``
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+Default: :const:`None`.
+
+Maximum time in seconds to wait when acquiring a connection or producer from
+the broker pool. When the pool limit is exceeded and this timeout expires,
+task dispatch raises :exc:`~celery.exceptions.OperationalError` instead of
+blocking indefinitely.
+
+Set to :const:`None` (the default) to wait forever. For example, setting this
+to a few seconds helps avoid stalled producers when all broker pool connections
+are in use.

 All of the above visualization functions share parameters to customize the visualization (e.g., hide legend, hide inputs). Learn more by reviewing the API reference for `Driver.display_all_functions() <https://hamilton.apache.org/reference/drivers/Driver/#hamilton.driver.Driver.display_all_functions>`_; parameters should apply to all other visualizations.
 
+Display names
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+By default, each node is labeled with its name and type. You can substitute a human-readable display name by adding a ``display_name`` tag to the function:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+    from hamilton.function_modifiers import tag
+
+    @tag(display_name="My Custom Display Name")
+    def node_with_display_name(input_a: int) -> int:
+        """A node with a custom display name for visualization."""
+        return input_a + 1
+
+    dr.display_all_functions()
+
+For nodes, label resolution uses an explicitly supplied name parameter first, then the ``display_name`` tag value, then the node's Python identifier. Input/dependency labels use the ``display_name`` tag when present and otherwise fall back to the node identifier. If ``display_name`` is a list, the first element is used; an empty list falls back to the node name. The resolved label is HTML-escaped before it is included in the Graphviz output, so special characters such as ``<``, ``>``, ``&``, and quotes render correctly.
+
 .. _custom-visualization-style:
 
 Apply custom style
